evidence.text: **What changed structurally.** [THE COMPANY] completed the **Millrose Properties** spin-off in Feb 2025 — $5.6bn of land / 87,000 homesites and $1bn of cash off the balance sheet — converting [THE COMPANY] to a land-light, just-in-time homesite model, with ~$900m of the cash contribution used by Millrose to take the Rausch Coleman land [37][38]. Q2 FY26 was described as the quarter that "tests the land-light model" [15]. The structure raises ROE in good times and, per the HousingWire framing, may *reduce* flexibility to slow production in bad ones because take-down schedules are contractual [26]. This is the least-understood part of the story and a plausible source of surprise in either direction.
